overall: No violation found: the June 22 meeting was cancelled, so the boilerplate notice could not support an insufficient-notice violation. The AG cautioned that future notices must be specific and reminded the Commission of complaint-response duties.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the topics listed on the June 22 meeting notice were insufficiently specific. The meeting was cancelled, so no violation was found.
allegations.key_passage: In this instance, we find that the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged in the complaint because the June 22 meeting was cancelled.

allegations.summary: The AG itself noted the Commission's response to the complaint did not follow 940 CMR 29.05(5), since it did not send the complainant a response or copy the AG. Not alleged by the complainant.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Commission met and discussed the complaint on July 6, which was within 14 days of receipt of the complaint, it did not send the complainant a response nor simultaneously provide the Attorney General with a copy of the complaint, a response and a description of remedial action taken.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
